# Kition kit rules (read first)

<!-- kition-quality:begin (generated by kition-sdk tools/sync-quality.mjs; edit the template there) -->
## Quality rules (read first)

- Tests are the spec. Read `docs/quality.md` and the feature catalogue (`features.yaml`)
  before changing behaviour. When code and a case disagree, the case wins unless a maintainer
  approves changing the case.
- Before you finish any task, run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`. If it fails, the task is not done. Claude Code
  runs it for you through the Stop hook; agents without hooks (Codex) run it by hand and
  report the real exit code.
- The full checks and tests run on GitHub, in the kit's CI run, not on your machine: a task is
  done only when HEAD has a passing CI run and is on `origin/main`. Use Kition's
  `scripts/kit-ci.sh` (`push`, `wait`, `failures`, `land`; Kition's `docs/kits.md`, section
  4c). Compile only the crates you touched locally.
- Never edit expected results to make a test pass: files under `cases/**/expected/`, paths
  listed under `protected` in `features.yaml`, and the `expected`, `tolerance`, `reference`,
  `input` and `steps` of an existing `case.yaml`. If you believe an expected result is wrong,
  stop and explain why in the task's findings; only a maintainer approves expected-result changes.
- Never weaken a test to make it pass: no deleted or loosened assertions, no added
  `#[ignore]`, `.skip`, `.only` or `.todo`, no raised tolerances. kition-sdk's
  `tools/check-expected.mjs` lists every such change for the maintainers.
- Every bug fix starts with a failing case under `cases/regressions/issue-<n>/`, then the fix.
- Every new feature adds an entry to `features.yaml` and at least one gating test.
- Put the task id and the case ids in the commit message.
- Stage only your own files: `git add` them by name; never `git commit -a` or `git add -A`.
  Other sessions may have uncommitted work in the same checkout.
- Commit on `main` in the repository's main checkout: no git worktrees, and one agent per
  repository at a time.
- Never start `cargo xtask eval` (the real-model `layer: eval` cases): only a maintainer starts it (F-QA-16). Write eval cases and check them with `--dry-run`, which calls no model.
- No compatibility layers: no aliases, old names, old file suffixes, migrations, or readers for
  old formats. Delete a replaced path in the same change.
<!-- kition-quality:end -->

This repository is Kition's `kit.layout` kit, not upstream. These rules come first; the
upstream rules below still apply to the engine.

- The kit draws **its own editor**: `web/` is a React app on `@kition/sdk/editor` (kition-sdk's
  shared kit UI library) with Kition Layout's menu bar, tool rail with flyouts, spread canvas, and the Pages, Layers, Swatches, and Styles panels; a host (Kition, or `web/dev.html` for development) shows it
  in an iframe and talks to it over the Kit UI protocol (`kition-kit-ui/1`, kition-sdk
  `docs/ui-protocol.md`). Style it only with the host's theme tokens and kit-editor components;
  ribbon labels and command titles are the upstream editor's English text, translated by
  `PHRASES` in `web/src/strings.ts` (the editor's own `en-US` and `zh-CN` strings). Files go only
  through the host.
- `bindings/wasm` compiles the engine to WebAssembly on the public `KitionAI/kition-sdk`
  crate; the editor runs it in a Web Worker. The contract and the Kition platform rules live in kition-sdk
  (`docs/platform/kits/engine.md`, `docs/platform/reference/ui-protocol.md`), the agent protocol
  in KHP ([`kitharness/kitharness`](https://github.com/kitharness/kitharness)); change them there, never here. `kition-layout-kit` must keep passing `kition_kit::testing::check_contract`,
  and `kit.json` must pass kition-sdk's `tools/check-manifest.mjs`.
- Tools run in the engine (`KitTools`); what upstream's canvas draws over the pages is returned as
  engine overlays (`src/chrome.rs`). Never draw editor chrome into the rendered pixels.
- A `.klayout` file holds the document's **content, not its history** (kition-sdk data model 7.3,
  rule M16b): `content.bin` is the replica's sealed content snapshot. Never write
  `LayoutSession::snapshot()` (the whole history) into a file: it is for the host's history store
  and new replicas. Hosts call `prepare_save` (which seals the replica) before `save`; a save of a
  replica nobody sealed answers `not-sealed: …`.
  Anything that needs earlier versions (premises, a fork at a version) reads them from the live
  replica's history, never from a file.
- The whole repository is Apache-2.0 ([LICENSE](LICENSE)); third-party notices are listed in `NOTICE`.
  Upstream is credited only in `NOTICE`; never write upstream names anywhere else.

# Kition Layout — instructions for agents

Kition Layout is a clean-room page-layout engine targeting Adobe InDesign parity — and superiority (speed, openness, agent control).

## Start every session here
1. Read `plan/STATUS.md` (current milestone, next task), then the task in `plan/execution-plan.md` and the relevant `plan/architecture.md` section. Behaviour reference: `plan/indesign/*.md` (`11-observed-ui.md` holds measured observations of the running app).
2. Follow the autonomous operation protocol (`plan/execution-plan.md` §7). Don't stop to ask unless §7 lists the decision as the user's.

`plan/` is gitignored (local only).

## Never crash
People trust Kition Layout with their layouts; a crash loses their work. **This outranks feature work**: never ship a feature through a panic path, and fix a crash before building on top of it. Standard: see `docs/kits.md` in the Kition repository and kition-sdk's `docs/platform/`.
- **No panics in non-test code:** no `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!`, `unimplemented!`; no `unsafe` (`unsafe_code = "forbid"`). The one exception is a provably infallible literal (a constant regex, `write!` to a `String`): `#[allow(clippy::expect_used)]` + `.expect("why it cannot fail")`.
- **Errors are `Result<T, E>`** through the crate's error type and `?` (`ok_or(..)?`, `let … else`, `if let`, `map_err` for context). An unfinished feature returns an "unsupported" error. Don't `unwrap_or_default()` where a silent default would corrupt a document; return an error.
- **Input-derived numbers are hostile** (files, commands, settings): `get()` instead of `[i]`/`[a..b]`, slice strings at char boundaries, checked/saturating arithmetic for lengths and offsets, no division by zero or NaN casts, cap input-sized allocations.
- **Bound recursion** (seen-sets or depth limits for nested or cyclic documents). **Locks:** `lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)` or an error; thread joins are `Result`s.
- **Last-resort guard:** escaped panics during command execution and file import/export become an error, never a lost document. It's a safety net, not a license.
- **Prove it:** every crash fix lands with a small synthetic regression test that panicked before the fix.
- Clean crates carry `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable)]`; new crates start with it. Tests may `unwrap` (`.clippy.toml`).

## Non-negotiables
- **Clean-room.** InDesign is installed on the dev machine and may be *observed* black-box: run it, use its UI with synthetic documents, take screenshots (by window id) stored only under `plan/indesign/screenshots/` (never committed). Never read, disassemble or copy anything inside the InDesign bundle (names/listings only), never copy Adobe icons, artwork, presets or wording beyond feature names, never commit files produced by InDesign. Never copy GPL/AGPL/LGPL code (Scribus, LibreOffice, Ghostscript…).
- **Assets:** no Adobe iconography or images — ever. Every asset is original / OSI / CC0 / redistributable CC and has a row in `docs/attribution.md` (`cargo xtask assets` enforces it). Prefer art generated in code.
- **Fonts live in [`KitionAI/kition-fonts`](https://github.com/KitionAI/kition-fonts)**, never in this repo: don't commit new font files (the Latin UI/document fonts already in `assets/fonts/` stay). It is an optional build input, never a `Cargo.toml` dependency: `KITION_FONTS_DIR=/abs/path/to/kition-fonts cargo build` makes `crates/support/fonts/build.rs` embed its fonts as `kition_layout_fonts::KITION_FONTS` (Japanese: BIZ UDPGothic for the UI, Mincho first for document text; web builds embed BIZ UDPGothic Regular only). Unset, `KITION_FONTS` is empty and the app uses its bundled and system fonts; code and tests must work that way (tests on its glyphs skip). Releases build with it.
- **Shared test corpora.** Never commit large binary fixtures to this repo; fetch them pinned by commit and sha256-verified, as `cargo xtask corpus` does for PngSuite.
- **Everything is a command.** User-visible behaviour = a command in `crates/engine/engine/src/cmd/*` (id, label, menu path, shortcut, params doc, `enabled`, `run`) + tests. Tools emit commands (Begin/Preview/Commit). The headless kit app and the kit's own editor both reach them through `Session::execute`.
- **Layering** is enforced by `cargo xtask layers`.
- **The UI is thin**: panels read engine state and act through `app.run(id, params)`. Colours come from `theme::Tokens`.
- **Rust only** (no handwritten JS/TS). **Never break wasm** (`cargo xtask wasm`).
- **Checks run in the kit's CI run** on GitHub, not on this machine. Locally, run only the fast checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check -p <touched crates> --all-targets`, the wasm `cargo check` (`cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p <touched crate>`) and `pnpm typecheck` in `web/`. The full checks (clippy, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo xtask ci` — fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests, assets, layers, wasm — and every `test:*` script of `web/`) run in the CI run that `.github/workflows/ci.yml` starts through Kition's reusable kit CI; add no other workflow, and never start the Package workflow (releasing is the owner's step). A task is done when the CI run of HEAD is green and HEAD is on `origin/main` (Kition's `scripts/kit-ci.sh push`, `wait`, `land`). One task id per commit (`M2.1: type tool caret navigation`).

## Running and looking at the kit
- `cargo build --release -p kition-layout` builds the headless kit executable Kition's agent runs.
- `cd web && pnpm install && pnpm engine && pnpm dev` serves the kit's own editor at `dev.html` for interactive, visual work.
- Shell gotcha: `mv`/`cp` are aliased interactive here — use `/bin/mv -f` / `/bin/cp -f`.
- Parallel agents: separate `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per agent; edit only the crates you own; delete your target dir when done (disk).

## Roadmap
`docs/gaps.md` (every known shortfall, from the feature catalogue), `docs/roadmap.md` (the order of work, by priority) and `docs/parity/target-app-parity.md` (each feature's status against InDesign) follow `features.yaml`; `docs/parity/parity-checklist.md` is the presence checklist (`cargo xtask parity`), beside the typography, file-format, UI, hardware and localization parity docs in `docs/parity/`. When work lands, update the feature in `features.yaml`, then the affected docs.
